To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ammonium nitrate accelerated degradation of cement based material generates a large capillary pore network and is responsible for an important increase of water permeability.
the chemical degradation of CEM I (portlandite dissolution) generates an increase of the capillary porosity and of water permeability.
the accelerated ammoniacal leaching of cement based material is governed by a diffusion and is responsible not only for the dissolution of portlandite but also for C-S-H decalcification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of an accelerated chemical attack on the evolution of water transport properties and pore structure of hardened cement paste and concrete.
the development of a model that will allow to simulate the effect of accelerated chemical degradation on the water permeability and the pore structure of cement-based materials.
the development of an experimental and modelling approach for the prediction of the water permeability evolution of cement based materials under accelerated degradation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accelerated chemical degradation of cement paste and concrete by ammonium nitrate solution is not a good model for the prediction of the long term behaviour of cement based materials in natural environments.
the accelerated ammoniun nitrate leaching process is responsible for a significant degradation of cement based material and for a large increase in water permeability.
the accelerated ammoniun nitrate leaching of cement based materials is a good approach to study the evolution of water transport properties and pore structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
accelerated leaching of cement based materials with ammonium nitrates is responsible for the formation of a large capillary pore size distribution and an increase in the water permeability.
the accelerated ammoniacal attack was not only responsible for portlandite decalcification but also for C-S-H decalcification and for a large capillary pore generation.
the accelerated leaching of CEM I (CEM II) cement based materials with ammonium nit rate generates an important increase in total poros ity and a significant increase in water permeab ility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water permeability can be used to assess the degradation state of cement based materials and that the evolution of permeability is mainly governed by capillary porosity.
the accelerated ammoni-um nitrate leaching is a useful tool for investigating chemical degradation mechanisms and their impact on transport properties.
the chemical degradation of concrete is responsible for the increase of water permeability.
